Gait asymmetry and uneven stride detection
TMJ (temporomandibular joint) release and jaw tension

common_hook_patterns: Before-and-after mobility testimonials ('I could feel the difference immediately')
List-style education ('3 signs your horse needs adjustment')
Problem-solution framing ('It's not the bit, it's the sacroiliac')
Performance-focused CTA ('Unlock your horse's full potential')
Evidence-backed benefit statements ('Restores proper neuromuscular function')
Rodeo-and-ranch credibility ('30+ years serving performance horses')
Preventative maintenance angle ('Don't wait until lameness shows')
dominant_visual_styles: Clinical close-up of hands-on adjustment/palpation during treatment
Horse in motion (walk/trot in-hand and under saddle) as proof of improvement
Practitioner with horse and rider at sunset/barn setting (rural-luxury framing)
Anatomy diagram overlays with highlighted problem areas (TMJ, sacrum, hock)
Testimonial video clips from satisfied rodeo/ranch owners
raw_summary: Across competitors in Texas, Montana, and nationally, equine chiropractors and bodyworkers are emphasizing performance optimization, injury prevention, and post-event/post-haul recovery. The rodeo circuit generates strong traction for practitioners like <cite index="30-6,30-9,30-10">Justin Beasley (VOM specialist working on bucking broncs and bulls)</cite>, while <cite index="1-1">Sport Horse Chiropractic (161K IG followers)</cite> focuses on stretching and mobility education. <cite index="41-1,41-2,41-3">Montana-based Balance Point Equine Bodywork serves ranch horses, rodeo athletes, and retirees using massage and myofascial release.</cite> <cite index="17-1,17-4,17-5">Heart and Hoof Chiropractic (Dr. Rhonda Parker, Texas) emphasizes building trust and evaluating horses 'from HOOF up to head and back to tail.'</cite> Educational hooks center on gait analysis, compensation patterns, and the link between spinal alignment and performance. Visuals typically feature hands-on clinical work, in-motion gait footage, and barn/rural settings. <cite index="36-1,36-2,36-3">A current competitive landscape shift: Texas is debating rule changes (April 2026 hearing) that could restrict equine chiropractic work to licensed veterinarians</cite>, positioning certified practitioners as higher-value partners.
